name: Linear Lichen Planus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Criteria for Linear Lichen Planus

criteria.description: Presence of violaceous, polygonal, flat-topped papules arranged linearly along Blaschko's lines
Skin biopsy showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermoepidermal junction with basal cell degeneration
No history of drug exposure known to induce lichenoid eruptions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical linear violaceous papules along Blaschko's lines with confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; exclusion of drug-induced lichenoid reactions is important.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Violaceous polygonal flat-topped papules arranged linearly along Blaschko's lines
searchTerms: polygonal purple skin spots arranged linearly

pathognomonic.symptomName: Wickham striae (fine white reticulations) overlying papules
searchTerms: fine white lines on skin bumps

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected linear lesions
Erosions or ulcerations secondary to scratching

occasional.symptomName: Nail changes including longitudinal ridging or thinning
Oral mucosal involvement with reticular white plaques
searchTerms: oral mucosa with reticular white plaques

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of excoriated lesions
Mild localized edema adjacent to lesions

rare.symptomName: Scarring or atrophy at lesion sites
searchTerms: scars or thinning skin at lesion sites
skin atrophy and scarring on rash areas

rare.symptomName: Pigmentary changes extending beyond lesion margins
searchTerms: skin color changes beyond lesion edges

rare.symptomName: Koebner phenomenon (lesions at sites of trauma)

laboratory: Negative direct immunofluorescence in most cases
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible mosaicism along Blaschko's lines
other: Histopathology: band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at dermoepidermal junction with basal cell degeneration and Civatte bodies

distinguishingFeatures: Lichen striatus typically occurs in children
Histopathology shows spongiotic dermatitis rather than lichenoid infiltrate
Lesions are smaller and less violaceous
Psoriatic plaques have silvery scale and Auspitz sign
Histology shows acanthosis and neutrophilic microabscesses

redFlags: Rapid progression of lesions with ulceration
Presence of systemic symptoms such as fever or malaise
Non-response to standard topical corticosteroid therapy
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
